title: A Wearable Electrochemical Biosensor for Salivary Detection of Periodontal Inflammation Biomarkers: Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Sensor with Deep Learning Integration.
ml_task: CNN regression of salivary MMP-8 concentration from EIS spectra rendered as two-channel images, plus a transfer-learned binary healthy/periodontitis classifier, for a MIP/GO wearable electrochemical biosensor.

evidence.U: U0. METHODS 'Statistical Analysis' reports 'All data were collected from at least three independent replicates (n ≥ 3) and were presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD)', i.e. wet-lab replicate spread, which section 7 excludes. Model results are point values (>= 99% and ~100% accuracy). No spread over folds/seeds, no per-prediction uncertainty.
evidence.E: E0. Looked in RESULTS AND DISCUSSION 'Implementation and Integration of Clinical Data'. The clinical classifier is itself fine-tuned on the clinical data ('a fine-tuning process was undertaken using a carefully curated and constrained clinical dataset'); no fixed model is evaluated on an untouched independent source, and the ELISA/Clarke-grid 'clinical validation' concerns the sensor, not the model.
evidence.EP: EP=0. The two E_prospective regex hits are 'computational and experimental validation of MMP-8 imprinting specificity' - DFT/MD predictions checked by FT-ATR and XPS. That validates the imprinting chemistry, not the ML model predictions on new samples.
evidence.S: S0, borderline S1. The lab-standard to clinical-saliva domain change is stated, but only the *adapted* model is scored ('TL achieved exceptional accuracy exceeding ≈99% within the initial epoch'; 'While both conventional training and TL methodologies attained ≈100% accuracy by the third epoch'). Section 7 counts transfer learning only if unadapted or few-shot-adapted performance on the new domain is reported, and the comparison made here is convergence speed vs training from scratch, both fitted on clinical data.

notes: Borderline S1 via transfer learning; flagged for adjudication. acknowledged_gap E and S: 'due to the relatively limited dataset size, further validation using extensive and diverse clinical cohorts is imperative to robustly establish the model's generalizability'. evidence.E: E0. Each task has its own model trained and tested on its own data; the rodent and porcine studies are separate pipelines, not a train-on-rat/test-on-pig evaluation. No public or literature dataset, no other lab or instrument.
evidence.EP: EP=0. No samples produced or measured after a model was fixed and compared with its predictions.
evidence.S: S0. Splits are ordinary train/test (solid vs dashed curves in Figures 3K and 5K). The 8-way-1-shot protocol is a few-shot training budget within one data source, not a shifted test distribution. The gait model labels are the 13 subjects themselves, so a cross-subject split does not apply.

notes: All four regex v1.1 candidates are the homonym 'conformal/conformally laminates' - false positives, as the pilot predicted for A3. Section parser fell back to BODY_OTHER for ~4350 words (PNAS layout), so I read the body headings directly. SI dependency: train/evaluation curves in SI Appendix Figs S13 and S22.

title: Passive Brain-Computer Interface Using Textile-Based Electroencephalography.
ml_task: Linear-kernel SVM classifying eyes-open vs eyes-closed cognitive state from four-channel EEG power-band features, for a fully textile-electrode passive BCI.

evidence.U: U1. TABLE caption in METHODS 2.5: 'Initial model selection cross-validation scores (mean ± standard deviation).' TABLE caption in RESULTS: 'Cross-validation results (mean ± standard deviation) using linear kernel SVM.' METHODS also compares 'the accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and fit time scores for each fold of the cross-validation procedure'. That is SD of model performance across ten folds. No per-prediction uncertainty, so U1.
evidence.E: E1, borderline. RESULTS: 'The generalizability assessment, which used the dry-electrode data to train the model and textile-electrode data to test the model, resulted in 92% accuracy and an F1 score of 92%, indicating strong cross-platform performance.' The fixed model is scored on data from a different instrument, which section 7 lists among the independent sources. The counter-argument is that the ten participants, lab and protocol are identical and only the headband differs, which would make it a same-lab batch and therefore E0.
evidence.EP: EP=0. No samples measured after the model was fixed; the study re-analyses an existing recording set.
evidence.S: S1, sub-code natural (cross-instrument). ABSTRACT: 'The SVM was applied to each EEG system separately and in a combined setting, where the classifier was trained on dry EEG data and tested on textile EEG data.' Performance of the unadapted model on the new sensor is reported (92% accuracy, F1 92%).

notes: E1 is the one call in this subset I would most like adjudicated: cross-instrument appears both in the E1 inclusion list and in the S1 'natural' sub-code list, and here the cohort and session are identical while only the electrode technology differs. I coded E1=1 on the literal wording and flagged it. S1 is unambiguous. The U2_gp regex hit is an Introduction sentence about other work (has [CIT]) - false positive.

title: Texture recognition based on multi-sensory integration of proprioceptive and tactile signals.
ml_task: Random forest and KNN classifying ten naturalistic textures from neuromorphic spike trains of a biomimetic fingertip (8x8 tactile array, piezoelectric and hydro-elastomer proprioception sensors) across six scanning speeds.

evidence.U: U0. RESULTS: 'the average performance across all 5 trials for each subset was computed and reported in Fig. 5' - the average only; accuracies are given as single numbers (99.9%, 88%, 82%, 72%, 92%). No +/- appears anywhere in the article, no error bars are declared, and there is no per-prediction uncertainty.
evidence.E: E0. All data are the 600 experiments run by the authors (6 speeds x 10 textures x 10 repetitions) on one biomimetic fingertip. No second source, no public dataset, no simulation-to-experiment step.
evidence.EP: EP=0. No samples measured after a model was fixed.
evidence.S: S0, considered carefully. Scanning speed varies, but RESULTS states 'The data samples were divided into 5 subgroups. Each time, one of these 5 subgroups was used as the test set and the remaining 4 subgroups formed the training set' over the pooled all-speed dataset, so every speed is inside the training distribution. There is no train-on-some-speeds / test-on-others evaluation, which is what a stated shift would require.

notes: Tempting S1 because of the 'irrespective of the scanning speed' claim in the Abstract, but the claim rests on pooled random 5-fold cross-validation, not a held-out speed. Flagged so the adjudicator can check Fig. 5 for undeclared error bars.
